episode.title: The Beauty of Finance

chapters.title: Introduction: Ajay is a Lot of Fun
Chapter 2: What Went Wrong in the Middle East?

episode.tagline: Human progress is enabled by the world of finance -- a world that seems dreadfully complicated from the outside. But once you understand its historical context, and how it evolved, everything about finance makes sense.
episode.about: In this episode, Ajay demystifies finance by giving us a guided tour of its history -- from primitive times to limited liability companies to banking to modern finance to derivatives. Finance is essential to our progress -- and yet, in India, we don't understand its beauty well enough, and the heavy hand of the state often messes things up. Amit then shares the insights of Timur Kuran on why the Middle East lagged behind in evolving financially and economically -- a story that truly will blow your mind!

items.content: Amit's opener: someone asked what Ajay is good at, Amit said 'Finance,' and they replied 'Finance and fun? What are you talking about?'…
Ajay: 'economics is the second most important thing in the world.' Amit: 'Wait, wait, wait. What is first? This is a family show.'

Amit recommends 'an obscure book' by 'Vijay Kelkar and Ajay Shah' and asks Ajay if he's heard of it. Ajay: 'Some obscure blokes. I think…
Ajay calls Amit a 'genius poker intellectual' in his algorithmic trading example. Amit says he 'started purring peacefully' at being…

'Wall Street tells Main Street what to do', the famous line Ajay uses to frame finance as the brain that guides the real economy.
John Hicks: the Industrial Revolution 'was as much about the stock market as it was about the steam engine', the invisible machine…
Merton Miller's description of banking as 'a disaster-prone 19th century industry.'
Chess player Levon Aronian called a chess game a conversation. Amit applies this to markets as 'a symphony of voices expressing opinions.'
The South Sea bubble and tulip mania, cited by Amit as the classic bubbles critics point to.
Ajay's evolution analogy for finance: 'Mother evolution did not design the eye, the eye evolved incrementally.'
Historian Bernard Lewis's thesis that the Islamic world was uncurious about the rest of the world, which Kuran rejects.
Timur Kuran taught Ajay personally in the late 1980s, when Ajay was studying in California.
